Georg Baselitz, a renowned German painter and sculptor, has died at the age of 88, as reported by Die Welt newspaper. Despite claiming a lack of talent and facing expulsion from art academies in his youth, Baselitz emerged as a pivotal artist in postwar Germany, celebrated for his provocative approach.

Born Hans-Georg Bruno Kern in 1938, Baselitz's upbringing was marked by the oppressive environments of Nazi Germany and later Soviet-occupied East Germany. His work, characterized by inverted landscapes and raw depictions of the human body, challenges traditional painting techniques and critiques the postwar societal landscape.

Baselitz's artistic journey included pivotal moments such as the 1963 controversy over obscenity in his paintings, which propelled him into the spotlight. His later works, marked by inversion, altered conventional perceptions of art. Despite controversy, including remarks on female artists, Baselitz remained a contentious yet influential figure in European art.
